bull_bear.body:
- Slide titled "Strengthening Our Balance Sheet": net debt Rs 4,719 Cr at Jun-26 vs Rs 4,824 Cr at Mar-26 - "Despite the capex, net debt reduced to Rs 4,719 Cr, supported by robust operational FCF".
- Debt mix shifted short to long: ST debt Rs 440 Cr at Jun-26 (vs Rs 1,060 Cr at Mar-26) and LT debt Rs 4,617 Cr (vs Rs 4,426 Cr); total debt Rs 5,057 Cr vs Rs 5,486 Cr.
- Leverage ratios improved: Net Debt/Equity 0.60x at Jun-26 vs 0.65x at Mar-26 (change -0.05); Net Debt/EBITDA 1.40x vs 2.86x (change 1.46).
- Shareholding stable at the top: Promoters 45.6% at both 31-Mar-26 and 30-Jun-26, with "FII + DII = 24.7% (vs 23.5%)"; deck's shareholder-value slide labels the market-cap series "CAGR 72% Value Creation" (Rs 669 Cr at Mar-20 to Rs 19,668 Cr at Jun-26, market cap as on the last day of the period).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in both the solvent (IPA) and acid (Nitric Acid) segments of Industrial Chemicals
- Around 45% share in India's merchant Nitric Acid market, supported by captive consumption for TAN and Ammonium Nitro Phosphate production
- Leading position in India's Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) market with an estimated ~40% market share; highest-ever TAN sales volume of 577 KT in FY2025-26 (up 11% YoY)
- Multi-location acid production facilities provide a supply-chain edge, especially serving major consumers in West and Central India
- Broad distribution network: 250+ channel partners and nearly 1,000 direct customers across 28 states/UTs, exporting to 23 countries
- Proprietary Nutrient Unlock Technology (NUT) in Crop Nutrition, differentiating Mahadhan's fertilisers via enhanced nutrient use efficiency
- Leadership position in water-soluble fertilisers in India, with strong presence in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka
- Backward integration across LNG-Ammonia-Nitric Acid-downstream value chain, reinforced by a long-term LNG supply agreement with Equinor, described as difficult to replicate
- PCL's captive ammonia production meets around 93% of the Group's ammonia requirement, with PCL also holding ~33% merchant ammonia market share in western India
- Post commissioning of the Dahej Nitric Acid expansion, DFPCL is positioned to become Asia's largest Nitric Acid producer
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on imported raw materials — Reliance on imported phosphoric acid, potash, and ammonium sulphate exposes the Company to supply chain vulnerabilities and currency risks.
- Working capital intensity and subsidy dependence — The working capital-intensive nature of the business, coupled with dependence on government subsidies, poses liquidity and financial risks.
- Weather / monsoon risk — Risk of below-normal rains due to forecast El Nino impact, which can affect Crop Nutrition demand.
- Geopolitical risk — Evolving trade policies can impact overall supply chain economics and trade balance.
- Regulatory change risk — Risk of sudden policy changes affecting operations, such as subsidy levels, state incentives, export quotas and import duties.
- Price pass-through lag — Delay in passing increased raw material prices to end customers may impact the Company's margins and profitability.
- Project execution / delay risk — Potential delays in regulatory clearances could affect timelines of capital projects such as the Gopalpur TAN plant and Dahej Nitric Acid expansion.
- Forex fluctuation risk — Absence of natural hedges exposes the business to forex fluctuations.

business.body:
- Three verticals (Mining Chemicals/TAN, Industrial Chemicals, Crop Nutrition) built on an "Integrated value chain of GAS to Downstream Products"; deck cites 40+ years experience, 6 manufacturing sites, 2,300+ employees and market capitalisation of "US$ ~2.07 billion (as on 30 Jun 2026)".
- Mining Chemicals: "India's only manufacturer of High Density, Low Density & Medical Grade Ammonium Nitrate", dominant market share (~39% domestic in TAN), plants on both East and West coasts, and value-chain integration "forward into explosives, backward into ammonia".
- Industrial Chemicals: "Largest manufacturer of Nitric Acid in South East Asia" and one of the leading manufacturers/marketers of Iso Propyl Alcohol; deck states domestic share of "62% in CNA, 27% in DNA, 10% in Merchant IPA".
- Crop Nutrition: "Market leader in specialty and water-soluble fertilisers in India", "India's only manufacturer of Prilled NP 24:24:0", "India's Largest manufacturer of Bentonite Sulphur", and the only producer of crop-specific NPK nutrient solutions with micronutrients and Nutrient Unlock Technology (NUT); 'Mahadhan' brand strong in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat.
- Deck's key takeaway slide: "Establishing market dominance through strategic initiatives", "Market leadership in most categories" and capex "strategically positioned for emerging opportunities".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger] Deck shows "Corporate Structure post Demerger" with DFPCL and MAL, listing Mining Chemicals (TAN), Crop Nutrition, Industrial Chemicals, Value Added Real Estate (VARE), Ammonia, subsidiaries CCPL (mining explosives) and DGCPL (LNG trading), plus blasting services in Australia; the deck does not explain the demerger terms.
- [Regulation - PESO] TAN production and dispatch were disrupted by "PESO ANRS portal changes", the stated reason for the 12% YoY volume decline.
- [Regulation - RGP quota] Government of India curtailed the RGP quota (linked by the deck to the US-Iran conflict), cutting IPA volumes 76% YoY and forcing a shutdown; outlook says relaxation of the quota improves supply availability "however, correction in domestic IPA prices is expected".
- [Demand outlook] Monsoon-driven slowdown in mining/infrastructure may hit Q2 TAN demand though elevated FGAN prices should support margin; for Crop Nutrition, El Nino impact expected to be limited with "only 12 of 44 core districts likely to receive below-normal rainfall".
- [Gas] Margin support attributed to an Equinor gas arrangement; the deck gives no contract volume, tenure or pricing.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: DFPCL is a diversified, multi-product organisation serving critical sectors of the Indian economy including mining, pharma & chemicals, infrastructure, and agriculture. It operates across four strategic business verticals - Industrial Chemicals, Mining Chemicals, Crop Nutrition Business and Value-Added Real Estate - with manufacturing facilities at Taloja, Dahej, Srikakulam, and Panipat, and a new facility at Gopalpur nearing completion. Following a strategic restructuring, Industrial Chemicals and Value-Added Real Estate sit under DFPCL itself, Mining Chemicals under Deepak Mining Solutions Limited (DMSL), and Crop Nutrition under Mahadhan AgriTech Limited (MAL).
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Industrial Chemicals:** Iso Propyl Alcohol (IPA), Nitric Acid (Weak/Concentrated/Strong), Ammonia, Liquid CO2, Propane, Hydrogen, Cororid, PuroGuard+, Purosolv (pharmacopeia-grade solvents: IPA, Methanol, Acetone, MDC), Pickbrite, Solar Grade Nitric Acid (SGNA), Pure DIPE
- **Mining Chemicals:** LDAN, HDAN, Melt, Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN), initiating systems, commercial explosives, blasting technology and technical services
- **Crop Nutrition Business:** Smartek (enhanced efficiency NPK fertilisers), Croptek (crop-specific balanced nutrition), Solutek (crop-stage specific water-soluble fertilisers), Bensulf Super-Fast (bentonite sulphur)
- **Value-Added Real Estate:** Creaticity (furniture and home decor, co-working spaces, F&B, sports and entertainment)

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body:
- Transitioning across the portfolio from products to solutions - specialty/crop-specific products and productivity enhancement in Crop Nutrition, application-led innovation in Industrial Chemicals, and a Total Cost of Ownership productivity-partner model in Mining Chemicals
- Forward integration into commercial explosives, initiating systems and mining services to become an integrated mining solutions partner spanning mining chemicals, explosives and mining services, reinforced by the Chardham Chemicals acquisition and 100% ownership of Platinum Blasting Services
- Backward integration of the value chain from LNG (via the long-term Equinor supply agreement) through Ammonia and Nitric Acid to downstream products, to strengthen supply security, competitiveness and margin resilience
- FY2025-26 marks a transition from a multi-year phase of capital investment and capacity creation to execution-readiness, followed by commissioning and scale realisation of the Gopalpur TAN and Dahej Nitric Acid projects during FY2026-27
- Crop Nutrition Business continuing its evolution from a commodity-led model to a science-driven, solutions-oriented platform built on proprietary Nutrient Unlock Technology, in-house R&D/agronomy and a DSIR-accredited Research & Innovation Centre
- DMSL continuing strategic investment in forward integration into commercial explosives/initiating systems and in Bulk-Mix-Delivery trucks to support its Total Cost of Ownership value-delivery model
- Dividend payouts follow the Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted 30 June 2017); for FY2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend of 100% i.e. Rs.10 per equity share, unchanged from the prior year, to be paid out of the year's profits subject to shareholder approval at the AGM.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: DFPCL is in the final stages of a multi-year capex cycle, transitioning from capacity creation to commissioning during FY2026-27. Two flagship projects are underway: a greenfield 376 KTPA Technical Ammonium Nitrate (TAN) plant at Gopalpur, Odisha (95% complete, 10 million safe manhours achieved) and a brownfield Nitric Acid expansion at Dahej, Gujarat adding 300 KTPA Weak Nitric Acid and 150 KTPA Concentrated Nitric Acid capacity (86% complete, over five million safe manhours recorded); both are in pre-commissioning/commissioning stages with commissioning expected in H2 FY2026-27. Separately, DMSL had already expanded its existing TAN capacity from 487 KTPA to 587 KTPA over the prior two years through brownfield expansion. DMSL continues strategic investment in forward integration into commercial explosives and initiating systems, and in Bulk-Mix-Delivery (BMD) trucks for down-the-hole ANFO delivery, to support its Total Cost of Ownership model. PCL's 1,500 TPD greenfield Ammonia plant produced 452 KT of ammonia in FY2025-26, meeting around 93% of the Group's ammonia requirement. In Crop Nutrition, the Company established a DSIR-accredited Research and Innovation Centre (RIC) at Pune, and in Value-Added Real Estate, Creaticity added new furniture/home-decor brands (Trezure Casa, Houslife, Edo Homes, Sleepy Cat, Morning Owl, Boingg Kids Furniture) plus fulfilment centres and a sports arena (Serve Society's Pickle and Padel courts) during the year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industrial/Pharma Chemicals outlook is guardedly positive: raw material and energy cost volatility and feedstock availability concerns may persist given geo-political scenarios, but strong demand is expected for Nitric Acid and Iso Propyl Alcohol on favourable growth in downstream pharma, agri, industrial manufacturing and mining
- A steadily expanding specialty chemicals portfolio continues to gain traction with key accounts, enhancing the resilience and relevance of the overall Industrial Chemicals business mix
- Mining Chemicals growth momentum is expected to continue, supported by government thrust on construction, power and infrastructure development, with resulting uptick in explosives demand across mining and infrastructure benefiting the TAN and Explosives growth strategy
- Mining Chemicals sales volumes grew 11% in FY2025-26, driven by robust B2C demand and improved customer engagement
- Crop Nutrition outlook is cautiously optimistic despite the possibility of a slightly below-normal monsoon influenced by El Nino; long-term demand is supported by increasing focus on crop productivity, balanced nutrition and soil health, with the Company prioritising key crops and expanding in irrigated and high-value segments
- Specialty and Croptek products contributed 33% of Crop Nutrition revenues, reflecting continued focus on differentiated and value-added offerings
- FY2025-26 profitability was impacted by elevated input costs, pricing pressures in Industrial Chemicals, limited subsidy realignment in fertilisers, and planned ammonia plant turnaround activities, partly offset by lower finance costs and operational discipline
- With improving market conditions and the two key growth projects (Gopalpur TAN, Dahej Nitric Acid) nearing completion, the Company sees itself as well-positioned for sustainable growth and long-term value creation
